episode.showDescription: Cougar Sports with Ben Criddle (@criddlebenjamin) keeps you up-to-date on all things BYU Sports. We not only cover football & basketball, but we dive into recruiting, baseball, soccer, and more. For insight that you can't get anywhere else, tune into 103.9/ 98.3 FM. Monday-Friday from 2-6 PM MST. Follow us on social media @espnthefan & interact with us using #ESPNTheFan.

transcript_window.text: We know over the last 30 years they've been the dominant conference.
NFL development, media rights, money, all those things, high -profile coaches, the pomp and circumstance surrounding college football.
I think that's waning a little bit in the new free market capitalistic era that we're seeing with the NIL and transfer portal, and you're not getting as much depth there.
I mean, we've seen it.
Look at their bowl record last year in the postseason.
And so my question to you is, we need more power four versus power four data points.
and the Aflac kickoff game is one of those Baylor versus Auburn, starting off Big 12 versus the SEC.
Let's discuss what type of game this is and why you guys were able to execute this, how you guys were able to execute this.
Well, I think you're exactly right, and it's really exciting for us.
This is one of only, to your point, one of only four P4 versus P4 games during the opening weekend.
So if you're looking for valuable data points, you're not going to get it from opening weekend because there aren't a lot of them.
But this is a great opportunity, and I think when you're talking about the P4 conferences especially, it's easy to compare the top quarter of the conference against each other.
You can look at the Big Ten and the ACC and see how they match up.
When you get into the depth is where it starts to get a little more complicated.
So I love to see teams who are, let's just say, middle of the conference, have every opportunity to win the conference, but you put an Auburn versus a Baylor, anything could happen.

and trying to find student athletes under the general same set of rules, you know, that neither one of them has a huge, you know, a huge booster that's going to walk in and help them create a $50 million roster.
So I agree with you.
I love the point that you're going to see now how a team like Auburn, who right now nobody really expects to compete for an SEC championship, but could with a Baylor.
games last year where it was like one score losses.
That's right.
And they were competitive.
They just couldn't find a way to win.
Yeah, and you get a kid like Lagway coming from Florida over to Baylor.
You know, it reshuffles the deck.
So I'm with you.
I love seeing games like this.
